gather-flint-desc: Flint lies loose on the ground in many places, among the other small stones. Pick up a few pieces: they're the start of every early tool. See the starter guide and the progression guide.
gather-sticks-desc: Sticks come from breaking bushes and fallen branches, and from the leaves of trees. Every early tool needs a handle.
forage-desc: Berry bushes grow in most places. Fill your belly while you work out the rest.
knap-axe-head-desc: Hold a piece of flint, then shift and right-click the ground to start knapping. Pick the axe head, and chip away the marked parts with left-click. See the knapping guide.
knap-knife-desc: A knife blade is knapped the same way as an axe head.
knap-spear-desc: A spear head, knapped like the rest, makes a weapon you can throw or stab with.
make-axe-desc: An axe head and a stick make an axe, in the crafting grid.
make-knife-desc: A blade and a stick make a knife. You'll use it for cutting grass, harvesting and skinning.
make-spear-desc: A spear head and a stick make a spear.
knap-shovel-desc: Knap a shovel head, then put it and a stick in the crafting grid. A shovel digs soil, sand and clay far faster than your hands.
chop-wood-desc: Fell a tree with the axe, then split the logs into firewood in the crafting grid, with the axe.
make-club-desc: A log and your knife make a wooden club in the crafting grid. It hits harder than bare hands, and doesn't break a precious spear.
cut-grass-desc: Cutting tall grass with a knife gives dry grass: kindling, bedding and much else.
gather-reeds-desc: Cattails grow in shallow water and on wet shores. Break them, faster with a knife, to get the tops; what's left keeps its root, and grows back.
first-hunt-desc: Chickens are easy prey. Larger animals fight back: keep your distance until you're better armed.
ground-storage-desc: Hold an item, then shift and right-click flat ground to set it down: up to four pots or bowls fit in a block, and firewood stacks into a pile. Tools lean against a wall with shift, ctrl and right-click. See the ground storage guide. Tick this off once you've stored something.
make-firestarter-desc: Two sticks and a little dry grass make a firestarter in the crafting grid. It's how you light fires until you have something better.
make-basket-desc: Ten cattails make a hand basket in the crafting grid. Put it in one of your bag slots for more room to carry.
hay-bed-desc: Eight dry grass make a hay block, and three hay blocks make a bed. Sleeping through the night is safer than wandering in the dark.
make-fire-desc: Shift and right-click the ground with dry grass to start a firepit, add four firewood, then hold right-click on it with the firestarter until it catches. Tick this off once it's burning.
build-shelter-desc: Five dry grass and four soil make ten blocks of cob in the crafting grid. Raise walls and a roof around your bed before the nights grow cold.
make-torch-desc: A stick and dry grass make a torch. Light it at a burning fire. Torches light the way at night and in caves.
cook-roots-desc: Break a cut cattail again to dig up its root, faster with a shovel. Roast the root on a lit firepit: it's plain, but it keeps you going when nothing else will.
find-clay-desc: Clay shows as patches of blue or red clay, often near water. Dig it with your hands or, faster, a shovel. See the clay forming guide.
form-bowl-desc: Hold clay, then shift and right-click the ground to start clay forming. Pick the bowl, and add clay with right-click and remove it with left-click, layer by layer.
form-pot-desc: A cooking pot is formed the same way. It's how you cook meals rather than single ingredients.
form-vessel-desc: A storage vessel holds more than any basket, and keeps food longer.
find-fireclay-desc: Fire clay lies in small patches at the surface where there's bauxite sand or gravel, and in large patches under coal seams. It stands far more heat than plain clay.
fire-pottery-desc: Raw clay must be fired before it's any use. Make a pit kiln: shift and right-click to set the raw pieces on the ground, add dry grass, sticks and firewood, and light it. Wait for it to burn out.
form-oven-desc: A clay oven is formed from fire clay, and needs a lot of it. It doesn't need firing in a kiln.
make-bricks-desc: Four clay make a raw brick in the crafting grid. Fire the raw bricks in a pit kiln. Fired bricks, set in mortar, build walls that last.
make-jug-desc: Form a jug and fire it. A jug carries water and other liquids, and with flour it makes dough.
make-watering-can-desc: Form a watering can and fire it. Fill it at water and use it on farmland that's too far from water to stay moist.
fire-pot-desc: Fire the cooking pot the same way, if it wasn't in the first kiln.
make-planter-desc: Form a planter, fire it and place it. Planters hold flowers and small plants wherever you set them, indoors or out.
place-vessel-desc: Fire the storage vessel and place it somewhere sheltered. Food keeps longer in a cool, dark place.
place-oven-desc: Place the oven. Fill it with three to six firewood, light it, and once the fire burns out the oven is hot: put in what you want to bake, and watch it doesn't burn.
make-shingles-desc: Form shingles from clay, twelve at a time, and fire them. They make a clay roof that won't rot or burn like thatch.
cook-meal-desc: Put the pot in a lit firepit with ingredients inside it, wait for it to cook, and take it out. A mixed meal fills you up far better than its parts.
roast-meat-desc: Put raw meat in a lit firepit and take it out once it's cooked. Cooked meat fills you up and won't make you sick.
serve-meal-desc: Hold an empty bowl and right-click a cooked pot to fill it, then eat from the bowl. A pot holds several portions. See the meal making guide.
make-dough-desc: Flour and a bowl or jug of water make dough, in the crafting grid.
make-table-desc: Seven boards make a wooden table in the crafting grid. Besides holding things, it's where pies are put together.
cook-stew-desc: A stew needs two portions of meat, and takes vegetables or eggs as extras. Every slot of the pot you use must hold the same number of portions.
cook-soup-desc: Pour a portion of water into the pot, then add vegetables, and meat if you have it. Soup stretches a few vegetables a long way.
cook-porridge-desc: Porridge is two to four portions of grain, with fruit, vegetables or honey as extras. Grain alone barely feeds you; as porridge it fills a bowl.
bake-bread-desc: Put dough in a hot clay oven. It bakes in stages: take it out once it's bread, before it chars.
bake-pie-desc: Shift and right-click a table with two dough to lay a crust, fill it with fruit, vegetables, meat or cheese, and add dough for a top. Bake it in a hot oven.
eat-well-desc: Your character panel shows five food groups: fruit, vegetables, grain, protein and dairy. Keeping all of them full raises your maximum health, so keep a varied larder.
knap-hoe-desc: Farming starts with a hoe. Knap a hoe head from flint, as you did the others. See the farming guide.
gather-seeds-desc: Wild crops grow here and there. Harvesting them gives seeds to plant.
make-compost-desc: Rotten food isn't waste. Seal 64 rot in a barrel and wait 20 days for 16 compost. Use it on farmland to add nitrogen.
make-hoe-desc: A hoe head and a stick make a hoe. Right-click soil with it to till it into farmland. The richer the soil, the better crops grow on it.
harvest-grain-desc: Plant seeds on tilled farmland, within three blocks of water if you can, or water it. Harvest when the crop is fully grown.
grow-vegetables-desc: Plant carrots, onions, turnips, parsnips or cabbages. Each crop draws on one of the soil's three nutrients, shown on the farmland's tooltip: rotate crops so the soil can recover.
make-quern-desc: A quern grinds grain into flour. Two sticks and four full blocks of granite, andesite, basalt or peridotite make one, with a hammer and chisel in the crafting grid. A rock block comes out whole once everything around it has been dug away.
grow-pumpkin-desc: A pumpkin plant spreads a vine, and the pumpkins grow on the ground beside it, so leave it room. Cut a pumpkin into slices with a knife in the crafting grid.
gather-saltpeter-desc: Saltpeter forms as a crust on the walls and floors of caves. Use it on farmland to add potassium.
grind-flour-desc: Put grain in the quern and turn it.
grind-bonemeal-desc: Grind bones in the quern. Bonemeal adds phosphorus to farmland.
full-harvest-desc: Keep several fields: grain, vegetables and flax, rotated and fertilized. Below 10°C crops grow slowly and below 0°C not at all, so the harvest before winter matters.
take-bush-cutting-desc: Wild berry bushes can't be moved: broken, they leave only debris. Hold a knife, then shift and right-click a bush for a cutting. Each bush gives one cutting a year.
take-tree-cutting-desc: Fruit trees grow wild in most climates. Break a branch off a living fruit tree to get a cutting. See the fruit trees guide.
make-flowerpot-desc: Form a flowerpot, fire it and place it, then plant a flower in it.
build-greenhouse-desc: Roof an area of up to 14 blocks a side with glass: at least half the roof must be glass blocks or slabs. The walls can be anything. See the greenhouse guide.
plant-bush-cutting-desc: Plant the cutting in ordinary soil, not farmland. It takes four to eight months to bear fruit. Unlike wild ones, your bushes take fertilizer, applied to the bush itself.
plant-tree-cutting-desc: Plant the cutting on soil. Only some planted cuttings take, so plant more than one. A fruit tree grows slowly, and fruits once a year.
greenhouse-bonus-desc: Farmland, fruit trees and berry bushes inside a greenhouse are 5°C warmer, which stretches the growing season. Tick this off when farmland inside shows the greenhouse bonus on its tooltip.
graft-cutting-desc: Place a cutting on the stub where you broke a branch off a tree. Grafts take more often than planted cuttings, and one tree can carry several kinds.
build-pen-desc: Livestock starts with a fence. Rough-hewn fences need only logs, sticks and an axe; plank fences come later. Enclose a patch of grass, then lure or chase animals inside. See the animal husbandry guide.
make-trough-desc: Three planks make a small trough, for chickens, hares and other small animals. Fill it with grain or vegetables: fed animals breed, and hungry ones lose weight over winter.
make-bucket-desc: Five planks and a rope or flax twine make a wooden bucket. It carries ten litres of any liquid: water, milk, brine or honey.
make-basket-trap-desc: A basket of cattail or papyrus tops and a stick make a basket trap. Bait it with food the animal likes and it may catch chickens, hares and many young animals.
make-crate-trap-desc: A reinforced crate trap is built from planks and bronze or better nails and strips. It catches larger animals than a basket trap, but tiny baits like grain won't do.
melt-fat-desc: Pigs, sheep, goats, deer, bears and raccoons leave raw fat when you harvest them. Cook it in a pot over the fire and it sets into lumps of rendered fat, used for pelts, the fruit press and sealing crocks.
make-cleaver-desc: Smith a cleaver blade and put it on a stick. A cleaver kills an animal from the third bred generation on in one blow.
make-large-trough-desc: Pigs, sheep and goats eat from a large trough, made from five planks. Animals are drawn to a full trough, which helps when herding them in.
make-henbox-desc: Five planks and dry grass make a henbox. Hens lay in it rather than on the ground, and a broody hen sits on three eggs until they hatch, if there's a rooster about and the hens are well fed.
breed-animals-desc: Keep a male and a female of the same kind in the pen and their trough full, and in time they have young. Animals bred this way grow tamer each generation. Tick this off when the first young are born.
collect-eggs-desc: Take eggs from henboxes or the ground. Leave three in a box if you want chicks instead.
milk-animal-desc: A ewe or nanny goat that has recently given birth can be milked: hold an empty bucket and use it on her. The more domesticated she is, the likelier she gives milk. Milk spoils fast, so drink it or make cheese.
raid-wild-hive-desc: Wild bee hives hang in trees and hide in hollow logs. Breaking one gives honeycomb, but angers the bees and ends that colony. Leave one standing if you want to catch a swarm.
make-skep-desc: A skep is woven from cattail or papyrus tops and sealed with clay, in the crafting grid. It's a home for bees.
plant-flowers-desc: Bees need flowers. Pick wild flowers and plant them near where your skeps will stand.
populate-skep-desc: Place an empty skep near a wild hive with flowers about, and in time a swarm moves in. Use a populated skep to pick it up into a free backpack slot, carry it home, select that slot with Ctrl and the scroll wheel, and place it down. See the animal husbandry guide.
harvest-honey-desc: When a skep is full, break it to take the honeycomb. That ends its colony, and the bees may turn on you. Bees make no honey in very cold weather.
expand-apiary-desc: A strong colony swarms into empty skeps placed nearby. Set out a few more beside it, with plenty of flowers.
squeeze-honey-desc: Hold honeycomb over an open container, such as a bowl or bucket, and squeeze it to get honey and beeswax. A fruit press does it faster. Each comb gives a fifth of a litre.
collect-beeswax-desc: Beeswax is what's left of squeezed honeycomb. It seals crocks, waxes cheese and makes candles.
make-candle-desc: Cook three beeswax and one flax fiber in a pot over the fire to make a candle.
make-pan-desc: A log and a knife in the crafting grid make a wooden pan. Stand in water, use the pan on sand, gravel or bony soil to fill it, then use it again to sift out nuggets and stones. See the panning guide.
make-charcoal-desc: Dig a pit, fill it with full stacks of firewood and cover it with blocks that don't burn, leaving the top of one stack open. Build a firepit on that stack, light it, and seal it within half an hour. See the charcoal burning guide.
find-copper-desc: Native copper sometimes lies on the surface as loose ore, and panning turns up nuggets too. Twenty nuggets make one ingot's worth of metal.
form-crucible-desc: Metal is melted in a crucible over a fire.
form-mold-desc: Molten metal is poured into a mold. Pick a tool to cast: a pickaxe is a good start.
make-tongs-desc: Sticks and rope make wooden tongs, in the crafting grid. Hold them in your off hand to handle a hot crucible or casting without burning yourself.
fire-metalwork-desc: Fire both in a pit kiln, as you did your other pottery.
cast-tool-desc: Put the fired crucible in a firepit, fill it with copper nuggets and heat it with charcoal until the metal melts. With tongs in your off hand, take it out and pour it into a mold, then wait for the casting to cool. See the smelting guide.
form-ingot-mold-desc: Ingots are how metal is kept and worked. An ingot mold casts two at a time.
make-shovel-desc: Cast a shovel head in a shovel mold and fit it to a stick. It digs soil, sand and gravel much faster than stone.
make-pickaxe-desc: With a pickaxe you can mine stone and ore.
cast-axe-desc: Cast an axe head in an axe mold and fit it to a stick. A metal axe fells trees much faster than flint.
make-hammer-desc: Cast a hammer head and put it on a stick. Smithing needs a hammer.
cast-ingot-desc: Fire the ingot mold, then pour molten copper into it.
build-forge-desc: Seven blocks of cobblestone make a forge; cobblestone is eight stones and a lump of clay. Fill the forge with charcoal and light it with a torch to heat ingots for smithing.
cast-anvil-desc: An anvil is cast in its own mold, from a lot of metal. With it you can smith.
first-smithing-desc: Heat an ingot in the forge until it glows, put it on the anvil, pick what to make, and hammer it into shape. See the smithing guide.
make-saw-desc: Smith a saw blade on the anvil and fit it to a stick. A saw cuts logs into boards, and boards open up carpentry.
smith-knife-desc: Smith a knife blade on the anvil and fit it to a stick. A metal knife lasts far longer than a stone one.
make-scythe-desc: Smith a scythe head and fit it to a stick. A scythe cuts grass and harvests grain over a wider area than a knife.
make-boards-desc: Put a log and the saw in the crafting grid to cut it into boards. Chests, barrels, doors and much else start here.
make-nails-desc: Metal nails and strips are smithed from an ingot on the anvil. Chests, lanterns and much else are held together with them.
make-oil-lamp-desc: Form an oil lamp from clay and fire it, then fill it with rendered fat in the crafting grid. It gives a steady light without a torch's smoke and ash.
make-chisel-desc: Smith a chisel on the anvil. With a hammer in your off hand, use it on a placed block to carve it into any shape, voxel by voxel.
grind-lime-desc: Limestone, chalk and marble grind into lime in a quern. Lime is the start of plaster, mortar and the limewater that soaks hides.
make-door-desc: Six boards of one wood make a door, in the crafting grid. Place it in a gap two blocks high.
make-ladder-desc: Boards and a stick make wooden ladders. Place them against a wall to climb it.
build-fence-desc: Boards and sticks make fences, and a fence gate lets you through. A fence keeps animals in and most creatures out.
make-roof-desc: Roofing comes in many kinds: thatch, sod over boards, boards alone, or clay shingles. Make eight pieces of any of them and put a roof over your head.
build-chest-desc: Eight boards around a set of nails and strips make a chest, in the crafting grid. It holds more than a basket, and stays where you put it.
cut-stone-bricks-desc: With a hammer and chisel in the crafting grid, polish a rock block, cut the polished rock into slabs, then cut a slab into four bricks.
burn-quicklime-desc: Heat lime in a firepit and take out the quicklime it turns into.
slake-lime-desc: Put four quicklime and a litre of water in a barrel to make slaked lime. Carry it away in a bucket.
make-plaster-desc: Quicklime and sand make a block of plaster, in the crafting grid. Plaster and boards together make patterned walls.
mix-mortar-desc: A litre of slaked lime and a block of sand in a barrel make four mortar.
lay-stone-bricks-desc: Eight stone bricks around one mortar make two blocks of stone brick, in the crafting grid. They build walls that last.
make-prospecting-pick-desc: A prospecting pick tells you what ore lies below. Cast its head in a mold or smith it, and fit it to a stick.
find-tin-desc: Tin comes from cassiterite, which is rare. Break three rock blocks with the prospecting pick, each 3 to 16 blocks from the others, and read the ore densities in chat; go where the reading is high. See the prospecting guide.
find-bismuth-desc: Bismuth comes from bismuthinite. Prospect for it as you did for tin. Break ore chunks into nuggets with a hammer in the crafting grid.
find-zinc-desc: Zinc comes from sphalerite. Prospect for it, mine it, and break the ore into nuggets with a hammer.
find-gold-desc: Native gold is rare. Prospect for it, and keep any nuggets you find.
find-silver-desc: Native silver is rare too. Prospect for it, and keep any nuggets you find.
alloy-bronze-desc: Melt copper and tin together in the crucible, nine parts copper to one of tin, and cast an ingot. Bronze is harder than copper.
alloy-bismuth-bronze-desc: Melt copper, zinc and bismuth together in the crucible: 50 to 70 percent copper, 20 to 30 zinc and 10 to 20 bismuth. Cast an ingot.
alloy-black-bronze-desc: Melt copper, gold and silver together in the crucible: 68 to 84 percent copper, and 8 to 16 each of gold and silver. Cast an ingot. Black bronze is the hardest bronze.
bronze-anvil-desc: Pour any bronze into the anvil mold. Nine ingots' worth of metal fills it.
bronze-pickaxe-desc: Cast or smith a pickaxe head in any bronze and fit it to a stick. It mines faster and lasts longer than copper.
smith-bronze-desc: Smith anything from a tin bronze ingot. Bronze tools last longer and work faster than copper ones.
bronze-axe-desc: Cast or smith an axe head in any bronze and fit it to a stick.
grow-flax-desc: Plant flax seeds in farmland and harvest the grown crop. Flax gives fibers as well as seeds and grain.
make-rope-desc: Rope is twisted from cattail or papyrus tops, or from wild vines, in the crafting grid. Tongs, ladders and much else need it.
make-woad-dye-desc: Put a woad flower and two litres of water in a barrel and seal it. Woad is a direct dye: it needs no mordant. See the dye making guide.
crush-alum-desc: Most dyes only hold on cloth treated with a mordant. Alum, crushed in a pulverizer, makes one; crushed cassiterite or chromite will do too.
make-yellow-dye-desc: An onion or a heather flower in a barrel with a litre of water makes yellow dye. Other plants and minerals give other colors.
spin-twine-desc: Four flax fibers make a length of flax twine, in the crafting grid. Twine also mends clothing a little.
make-linen-desc: Four lengths of flax twine make a piece of linen, in the crafting grid.
make-sewing-kit-desc: Flax twine and a stick make a sewing kit. Some clothes need one, and it mends worn clothing and armor.
make-sack-desc: Linen and flax twine make a sack. Wear it in a bag slot to carry more.
make-cloth-desc: Linen and a stick make plain cloth, in the crafting grid. Clothes are sewn from cloth.
sew-shirt-desc: Plain cloth makes a simple shirt, in the crafting grid. Clothes keep you warm and add up over a cold night.
sew-pants-desc: Plain cloth makes homespun pants or braies. A few need flax twine or a sewing kit as well.
dye-woad-desc: Seal plain cloth in a barrel with two litres of woad dye, and wait for it to turn blue.
mordant-cloth-desc: Put crushed alum and five litres of water in a barrel to make diluted alum. Then seal plain cloth in it to make mordanted cloth.
dye-cloth-desc: Seal mordanted cloth in a barrel with two litres of yellow dye. The finer clothes call for dyed cloth.
get-hide-desc: Butcher a killed animal with a knife to get its hide. Bigger animals give bigger hides, which make more leather. See the leather making guide.
make-limewater-desc: Put lime and water in a barrel, one lime to a litre. Diluted borax works the same way, if you find borax.
weak-tannin-desc: Seal an oak or acacia log in a barrel with ten litres of water for a day.
salt-hide-desc: Raw hides rot. Salt one in the crafting grid to keep it until you're ready to soak it.
soak-hide-desc: Seal a raw or salted hide in a barrel of limewater for about a day. Small hides need two litres, bigger ones more.
strong-tannin-desc: Seal another oak or acacia log in a barrel with ten litres of weak tannin for a day.
oil-hide-desc: Rendered fat and raw hides make oiled hides, in the crafting grid. Fat is rendered in a cooking pot. This keeps the fur on.
scrape-hide-desc: Put the soaked hide and a knife in the crafting grid to scrape it.
cure-pelt-desc: Leave the oiled hide for two days and it cures into a pelt. Pelts make fur clothes, bellows and the hunter's backpack.
prepare-hide-desc: Seal the scraped hide in a barrel of weak tannin for three days.
fur-hat-desc: A pelt and flax twine make a fur hat, in the crafting grid, with a knife. It keeps your head warm through the winter.
make-leather-desc: Seal the prepared hide in a barrel of strong tannin for four and a half days. Larger hides give more leather.
make-backpack-desc: Eight leather make a backpack, in the crafting grid. Wear it in a bag slot: it holds far more than a sack.
leather-boots-desc: Leather and flax twine make boots, in the crafting grid. They keep your feet warm.
tap-resin-desc: Resin leaks from the trunks of pine and acacia trees. Right-click a leaking log to collect it; it grows back in time. Rotors, gears and toggles all need it.
make-sails-desc: Sails are linen stretched on support beams and sticks. Saw a debarked log into a support beam, then craft the sails; a recipe makes four.
smith-pulverizer-metal-desc: A pulverizer needs metal: two pounder caps of bronze or better to strike with, and a metal plate for its toggle. Smith them on the anvil.
form-helve-mold-desc: Clay form a helve hammer head mold and fire it like your other tool molds.
make-rotor-desc: Craft a wooden windmill rotor from two upright logs, resin and rendered fat, with a hammer and a chisel in the grid.
make-axle-desc: Craft an axle from an upright log and rendered fat, with a hammer and a chisel in the grid. Axles carry power in a straight line.
make-gears-desc: Angled gears turn power around a corner. Craft them from a log, sticks, resin and rendered fat, with a saw, a hammer and a chisel.
cast-helve-head-desc: Pour bronze or a better metal into the fired helve hammer mold, then break the head out once it cools.
build-windmill-desc: Place the rotor on a tower or the side of a tall building: it needs at least 5 blocks of clear space, and higher gets more wind. Right-click it with sails to fit them; each set of 4 adds power. See the mechanical power guide.
make-pulverizer-parts-desc: Craft two pounders from logs, and a pulverizer toggle from an axle and a metal plate.
make-helve-desc: Fit the head to a handle of boards in the crafting grid.
connect-power-desc: Place axles from the back of the rotor toward where you'll work, and angled gears wherever the line has to turn. Keep windmills well apart: turbulence cuts their power.
build-grinding-wheel-desc: Craft a grindstone from sandstone, claystone or chert, then a grinding wheel from it with boards, an axle and nails and strips. Put it on a powered shaft and use it to sharpen blades for a short boost in power.
power-quern-desc: Place a quern so the shaft meets its top or bottom. With a full set of sails it grinds on its own. Put a hopper on top to feed it, and chests or hoppers beside it to catch what it drops.
build-large-gear-desc: Craft four large gear sections into a large wooden gear and lay it flat. Meshed with small gears it trades speed for torque, or joins the power of several windmills.
make-pulverizer-desc: Craft the frame from boards and a stone with a saw, and place it beside a powered axle; it needs plenty of headroom. Add the toggle, both pounders and their caps.
build-helve-hammer-desc: Craft a helve hammer base and a wooden toggle. Power the toggle from the side, place the base in front of it and an anvil of bronze or better 2 blocks from the toggle, then fit the hammer to the base. It hammers plates and iron blooms for you, but not tools.
crush-quartz-desc: Put quartz in the powered pulverizer and collect the crushed quartz. Bauxite crushes the same way; you'll need both for refractory bricks.
build-bellows-desc: Iron needs more heat than a forge gives on its own. Craft bellows from leather, boards and nails and strips, place them against your forge, and right-click them to pump air into it. They don't work on a firepit.
find-iron-desc: Limonite is a common iron ore. Hematite and magnetite are iron ores too, if that's what you find instead.
find-borax-desc: Borax is found in sedimentary rock. Grind it in a quern into powdered borax, the flux that welds iron.
find-meteorite-desc: Meteoric iron is rare: watch for meteorite blocks as you explore and mine. Break one for iron meteorite pieces and keep them until you have an iron anvil to work them on.
fire-fireclay-bricks-desc: Craft raw fireclay bricks from fire clay in the grid, then fire them in a pit kiln.
build-bloomery-desc: Iron can't be melted in a crucible. It's reduced in a bloomery: craft a base and a chimney from fireclay bricks, place the base and stack the chimney on it.
make-bloom-desc: Fill the bloomery with iron ore nuggets and coal or charcoal, then light it. After about a day it stops burning; break it to get the bloom.
refine-bloom-title: Work the bloom into an ingot
refine-bloom-desc: Heat the bloom in a forge with the bellows going, and hammer it on a bronze or better anvil to drive out the slag.
smith-iron-desc: Heat an iron ingot well, then smith it on the anvil. Iron tools outlast bronze ones.
smith-tongs-desc: Tongs let you carry things too hot to hold, such as a work piece fresh from the forge or a kiln's load.
coat-head-desc: Put an iron tool head, before it has a handle, in the crafting grid with fire clay. The thin clay coat makes quenching improve durability instead of power.
smith-anvil-parts-desc: Ferrous anvils can't be cast. Smith an anvil base and an anvil top from iron on your bronze anvil.
build-waterwheel-desc: Smith two small 4-way iron hubs and fit them to an axle. Place it above or beside fast-flowing water, high in the hills, then follow its tooltips to build the full wheel.
build-metal-windmill-desc: A metal rotor, made from iron rods, heavy brackets and support beams, carries large sails and can be twice as wide as a wooden one.
quench-head-desc: Heat an iron tool head into the range its tooltip shows, then right-click water with it to cool it fast. Let it cool slowly in the air from a lower heat to temper it. See the quenching guide. Tick this off once you have.
fuse-anvil-desc: Place the hot anvil base on the ground, put borax on it, set the hot top on that and strike it several times with a hammer. Tick this off once the anvil stands.
smith-meteoric-desc: Meteoric iron can only be worked on an iron anvil or better. Its tools last about a fifth longer than iron ones.
find-quartz-desc: Quartz veins run through rock underground, and loose pieces mark them on the surface. Ordinary fuels can't melt it; a bloomery can.
mold-refractory-desc: Craft raw refractory bricks from two fire clay, crushed quartz and crushed bauxite. Adding crushed olivine, then ilmenite, makes tougher tiers.
lay-fireclay-bricks-desc: Craft fired fireclay bricks with mortar into brick blocks. A coke oven is built from these, or from refractory bricks.
smith-hatch-desc: Smith an iron hatch door on the anvil. A coke oven needs one, and a beehive kiln needs three.
make-lantern-desc: Craft a lantern from clear quartz, a candle, a metal plate and nails and strips. Clear quartz sometimes drops when you mine quartz. A lantern gives a steady light.
make-glass-desc: Fill the bloomery with quartz and fuel, light it, and break it when it's done. Glass makes windows and greenhouses.
fire-refractory-desc: Fire the raw refractory bricks in a pit kiln, as you did the fireclay ones.
build-coke-oven-desc: Build a 3 by 3 by 3 cube of fireclay or refractory brick blocks, hollow in the middle and open on one side of the middle. Place the hatch door in that opening. See the coke oven guide.
make-panes-desc: Frame a glass block with boards and a lead ingot to get four leaded panes. Lead is smelted from galena.
lay-refractory-desc: Craft fired refractory bricks with mortar into refractory brick blocks. Furnaces and kilns are built from these.
make-gratings-desc: Craft fired bricks with mortar into gratings, which let heat rise through a floor. Fireclay gratings work too, but wear out faster.
make-coke-desc: Fill the oven's hollow with black or brown coal, light it with a torch and close the door. In 12 hours the coal becomes coke, which burns hotter than coal.
make-kiln-door-desc: Craft a kiln door from fired bricks, iron rods and iron nails and strips.
build-kiln-desc: Place the kiln door and ctrl-right-click it to see where every block goes. The 3 by 3 floor is nine gratings, and each other wall takes a hatch door. See the beehive kiln guide.
fire-kiln-desc: Load clay items on the gratings, put fuel under every grating, light it and close the door. Open hatches darken the ceramics. Take the hot results out with tongs, then tick this off.
lay-furnace-floor-desc: A cementation furnace stands on a 3 by 2 floor of refractory brick gratings. See the steelmaking guide.
build-furnace-desc: Craft two stone coffin sections and two lids from granite, andesite, basalt or peridotite. Place both sections on the middle of the grating floor, facing each other. Turning blister steel into steel needs your iron anvil.
make-iron-door-desc: Craft a solid or windowed iron door from iron plates. The furnace needs one.
stock-iron-desc: One firing takes 16 iron ingots. Gather them before you fill the coffin.
wall-furnace-desc: Shift-right-click the stone coffin to see where the bricks and the door go, then build them. It takes about 65 refractory brick blocks. Keep the air paths inside clear.
blister-steel-desc: Fill the coffin with the iron ingots and charcoal or coke, and close it with the lids. Dig a space two blocks under each section, fill it with a pile of coal and light it. Relight the piles about once a day; after about a week, break the coffin.
forge-steel-desc: Work the blister steel on an iron anvil into a proper steel ingot.
smith-steel-desc: Steel tools last about two and a half times as long as iron ones.
make-steel-tools-desc: Smith a steel pickaxe head and axe head, and put each on a stick in the crafting grid.
coat-steel-head-desc: Coat a steel head in fire clay, then quench and temper it as you did with iron.
make-steel-anvil-desc: Smith a steel anvil base and top on your iron anvil, and weld them together with borax as before.
find-salt-desc: Salt is ground from halite in a quern. Halite is found in some rock layers, and traders often sell salt. See the food preservation guide.
make-barrel-desc: Three planks and four sticks make a barrel. Put things in, seal it, and wait: it cures meat, pickles vegetables, ferments drinks and soaks hides.
form-crock-desc: Form a crock from clay. It holds a meal or pickles for a long time.
make-shelf-desc: Four planks make a shelf. Crocks and cheese wheels sit on it, which keeps a cellar tidy.
build-cellar-desc: Any fully enclosed space of soil, stone or brick stays cool all year. The smallest is a two-deep hole with a container in it, covered over; a larger one can be up to 7x7x7 with a door. Look at a container inside: its info shows how fast food spoils there. Tick this off when it shows the cellar working.
cure-meat-desc: Put raw meat or fish in a barrel with two salt for each piece, and seal it. After about twenty days it's cured, and keeps for about a year.
make-brine-desc: Pour water into a barrel, add one salt for every two litres, and seal it. Take the brine out with a bucket.
fire-crock-desc: Fire the crock in a pit kiln, as you did your other pottery.
pickle-vegetables-desc: Put vegetables in a barrel with a litre of brine each, and seal it. They take about two weeks. Pickled vegetables keep far longer than fresh, and curdle milk for cheese.
seal-crock-desc: Place a crock on the ground and fill it with a meal from a cooking pot or with pickles. Then use rendered fat or beeswax on it to seal it: food in a sealed crock spoils ten times slower. Tick this off once it's sealed.
stock-cellar-desc: Place sealed crocks in the cellar, on the floor or on shelves. Cold, dark and sealed together keep food longest.
collect-milk-desc: Cheese starts with 20 or 25 litres of milk in a barrel. Milk your animals until you have a full bucket, and pour it in. See the cheese making guide.
curdle-milk-desc: With 20 or 25 litres of milk in a barrel, add one pickled vegetable and seal it. In about three days the milk curdles.
make-cottage-cheese-desc: Add salt to the curdled milk and seal the barrel again. A day later it's cottage cheese. You can eat it from a bowl, or go on to make a cheese wheel.
press-cheese-desc: Use linen on the barrel to take out the cottage cheese. Place the bundle on the ground, add a stick, and twist it until the whey is gone. Open it and add five salt. Tick this off when you pick up the salted raw cheese.
wax-cheese-desc: Salted raw cheese and beeswax in the crafting grid make a waxed raw cheese, which keeps better while it ripens. Set it on a shelf, and about two weeks later it's waxed cheddar.
age-cheddar-desc: Set a salted raw cheese on a shelf and leave it. About two weeks later it's cheddar.
age-blue-cheese-desc: Raw cheese left to ripen in an enclosed space with no daylight and at least one opening to the outside, like a cold cave, becomes blue cheese instead.
make-metal-rod-desc: The fruit press turns on a metal rod. Smith one from an ingot of copper or better.
gather-resin-desc: Some old pine and acacia trunks leak resin. Harvest it with the use key and leave the log standing: it leaks again. Trees grown from saplings never have it.
find-lead-desc: Galena is lead ore, often found with silver. A prospecting pick shows where it lies.
make-soldering-iron-desc: A copper chisel and a stick make a soldering iron, which joins the metal plates of a still.
make-copper-plates-desc: The boiler and condenser are built from copper plates, smithed from copper ingots on the anvil.
make-fruit-press-desc: Planks, a metal rod, resin and rendered fat make a fruit press, crafted with a hammer and a chisel. See the brewing and distilling guide.
alloy-solder-desc: Melt lead and tin together in equal parts in the crucible, and cast an ingot.
press-juice-desc: Fill the press with fruit, put a bucket or other container under the spout, and screw it down. Fresh juice spoils, so ferment it soon.
cut-solder-desc: Saw a lead solder ingot into five bars, in the crafting grid.
ferment-drink-desc: Seal fruit juice, honey, or flour with water in a barrel. Juice turns to cider or wine in about a week; honey becomes mead and flour becomes ale in about two.
make-boiler-desc: Copper plates and lead solder bars, joined with the soldering iron, make a boiler. Place it over a firepit; it burns only firewood.
make-condenser-desc: Copper plates and solder make a condenser too. Set it beside the boiler, fill it with water, and put a bucket under its spout.
distill-spirit-desc: Fill the boiler with up to 30 litres of a fermented drink and light the fire under it. What drips into the bucket is a spirit: brandy, whiskey or vodka.
aqua-vitae-desc: Run a spirit through the still a second time to get aqua vitae, nearly pure alcohol, used in making other things.
stock-firewood-desc: Winter is long and cold. Keep plenty of firewood where you can reach it, under a roof.
stock-grain-desc: Nothing grows in winter. Keep grain in storage vessels, for bread and porridge and to fill the troughs.
cellar-food-desc: Store vegetables in your cellar. Raw vegetables keep best in a storage vessel there.
make-pelt-desc: Put rendered fat and raw hides together in the crafting grid to oil them. Oiled hides cure into pelts over a few days, wherever you keep them.
dress-warm-desc: Pelts and a knife make fur clothing in the crafting grid: gloves, a wrap, a coat. Warm clothes keep the cold off in winter.
winter-larder-desc: Before the snow comes, gather cured meat and pickles that will last until spring.
make-wormgrunter-desc: A stick and your knife make a worm grunting stick. Hold it with a stick in your offhand and Shift + right-click bare soil to scare worms up; wet climates have more, and none come when it's freezing.
make-fishing-pole-desc: Three sticks and three rope (or flax twine) make a simple fishing pole, in the crafting grid.
make-oar-desc: Two logs and two rope make a crude oar. You need it in your active hotbar slot to move a raft.
make-raft-desc: Twelve logs and three rope make a raft, in the crafting grid. Bamboo stakes work as well as logs.
make-rollers-desc: A sailboat starts on roller logs: three firewood make one, and you need five. Read the sailboat building guide before you start.
make-plumb-square-desc: Two sticks, flax twine and a stone make a plumb and square. The boat needs two.
bait-pole-desc: Put bait with the pole in the crafting grid. Worms catch small fish; stinkbait, cooked in a pot from water, fennel or licorice and dough or meat, catches small and medium ones; raw meat and small fish draw the largest.
ride-raft-desc: Right-click to place the raft on water, then right-click it to board. Row with the oar in hand, Shift to get off, and Shift + right-click to pick it up again.
catch-fish-desc: Right-click to cast into a large body of water. When the bobber goes under, right-click again to set the hook. If nothing bites, try other bait or another spot. See the fishing guide.
build-sailboat-desc: Select the rollers, turn the preview with the tool mode key and place them on flat ground with the blue strip in water. Then add what the boat asks for: logs and boards of one wood, firewood, the plumb and squares and rope. Launch it and sit at the tiller to sail.
fillet-fish-desc: Place a fish on the ground with Shift + right-click, then hold right-click on it with a knife to cut it into fillets.
make-ratlines-desc: Fourteen rope make ratlines. Attach them beside the mast with Ctrl + right-click to climb to the top.
make-boat-seat-desc: Five boards make a boat seat. Place it in one of the cargo spots with Ctrl + right-click to carry more passengers.
make-anchor-desc: A rock, firewood and twelve rope make a stone anchor. It goes in the front-left spot of the prow.
cook-fish-desc: Cook fillets on a firepit, the same way as meat. Larger fish give more fillets.
smith-nails-desc: Smith metal nails and strips on the anvil. A crate trap needs bronze or iron ones; tack takes any metal.
make-saddle-desc: Leather and two nails and strips make a saddle. See the guide to mountable animals.
trap-elk-calf-desc: Bait the crate trap and set it where elk graze; adult elk are too big for it. Right-click a full trap to carry it, and release the calf at home within a day, or it dies. Tick this off once you have one.
make-bridle-desc: Leather and nails and strips make a bridle. A snaffle bit steers like walking; with a curb bit, press forward once to go and again to stop.
break-in-elk-desc: Feed the calf well for a year and it grows into a partly tamed elk. Put the saddle on it and ride until it throws you, again and again, until it's tame.
ride-elk-desc: Bridle your tamed elk and ride it. It's faster than walking and carries tack for the road.
make-saddlebags-desc: Leather and nails and strips make saddlebags. They go over the elk's haunches and carry extra goods.
make-bone-flute-desc: Carve a bone with your knife in the crafting grid. Playing the flute calls your mount to you, as long as it's in a loaded area.
make-pillion-desc: Leather makes a pillion cushion. It goes behind the saddle and lets a second person ride, though only the front rider steers.
smith-falx-desc: Smith or cast a falx blade, then put it with a stick in the crafting grid. It's a far better weapon than a spear in close fighting.
knap-arrowheads-desc: Arrowheads are knapped from flint like any other stone tool head.
make-bow-desc: Three sticks and three rope make a crude bow; flax twine makes a simple bow instead. Hold right-click to draw and release to shoot.
make-sling-desc: Rope with leather, linen or a pelt makes a sling. It throws the stones in your inventory.
make-crude-shield-desc: Six sticks and three cattail tops, papyrus tops or bamboo stakes make a crude shield. Hold it in your offhand and Sneak to block. See the armor guide.
make-improvised-armor-desc: Firewood, rope and dry grass make improvised body armor, with a knife in the crafting grid. It breaks after a few hits, but it can save your life.
make-jerkin-desc: Leather makes a jerkin. It's light armor on its own and the base of brigandine and chain.
make-gambeson-desc: Layers of linen make gambeson armor. It takes a great deal of linen, but protects well without slowing you much.
make-arrows-desc: An arrowhead and a stick make a crude arrow. Add a feather for a better one.
make-bowstave-desc: Saw two logs into a long bowstave in the crafting grid. Leave it on a tool rack, or in your inventory, until it's dry.
make-round-shield-desc: Smith a bronze hoop and boss, then put them in the crafting grid with three boards.
make-wood-lamellar-desc: Firewood, pelts and resin make wooden lamellar. It protects more than improvised armor and costs little.
make-leather-armor-desc: Leather and flax twine make sewn leather armor: a good balance of protection and freedom to move.
make-brigandine-desc: Smith metal plates and fix them onto a leather jerkin in the crafting grid. Brigandine is heavy but protects well. Copper, bronze or iron will do.
make-longbow-desc: A dry long bowstave, flax twine, leather and fat, resin or beeswax make a longbow. It shoots farther and harder than a simple bow.
make-copper-lamellar-desc: Cast copper lamellae in a lamellae mold, then lace them onto pelts in the crafting grid.
make-chain-armor-desc: Smith chain and put it on a leather jerkin. Chain takes effort to smith, but it protects well and stays light.
make-scale-armor-desc: Smith metal scales and fix them onto chain armor of the same metal. Scale is close to impenetrable, and heavy.
make-plate-armor-desc: Smith metal plates and fix them onto chain armor. Plate is the highest tier of all.
make-steel-plate-desc: Steel plate armor makes you nearly invulnerable, but slow. Carry plenty of food. Heads and legs have their own pieces of every armor.
find-rusty-gears-desc: Rusty gears turn up in ruins, in bony soil when you pan it, and on drifters. Traders take them as money.
mine-stone-desc: Dig into the rock with a pickaxe. Each area has its own layers of stone; see the rock strata guide.
kill-drifter-desc: Drifters come out of the dark, deep underground and from rifts. Killing one restores a little of your temporal stability. See the temporal stability guide.
relight-fire-desc: Rain and snow put out firepits, torches and forges and cool hot metal. Relight a doused fire with a torch, and roof over the ones that matter. See the weather guide. Tick this off once you have.
make-poultice-desc: Four horsetail and two cattail or papyrus tops make a poultice. Hold it and right-click to heal your wounds.
make-bandage-desc: Cut linen with a knife, or twist two flax twine together, to make a clean bandage. Hold it and right-click to heal.
visit-trader-desc: Traders camp in wagons around the world. Right-click one to see what they sell and buy, and pay in rusty gears.
find-limestone-desc: Limestone is sedimentary, so it only lies above the metamorphic and igneous layers. If the top layer is igneous, other than basalt, look elsewhere; if it's sedimentary, check the caves below.
find-temporal-gear-desc: Temporal gears are rare: drifters sometimes drop one. Hold it in your offhand, a knife in your main hand, and hold right-click to turn it into temporal stability, at a cost in health.
survive-storm-desc: The chat warns you when a temporal storm is coming. Stability drains and drifters swarm while it lasts, so find shelter and light. Tick this off once one has passed.
soak-bandage-desc: Soak a clean bandage in spirits: put it with a bowl or jug of spirits in the crafting grid. A soaked bandage heals more.
no-quests: No quests are loaded. Quest packs add chapters under assets/<domain>/questline/chapters/.
pick-a-quest: Click a quest to see its tasks and rewards.
task-checkbox: Read this and tick it off
party-off: Parties are turned off on this server.
party-none: In a party, everyone's work counts towards party quests, and each member claims their own rewards. Start one, or join a party you've been invited to.
party-shares: Party quests count everyone's work. Each member claims their own rewards.
mode-party: Party quest: your party's work counts.
mode-party-alone: Party quest: in a party, everyone's work would count.
mode-server: Server quest: everyone's work counts, and each player claims once.
mode-server-first: Server quest: everyone's work counts, and the first to claim takes the reward.
pins-full: You can pin {0} quests at most. Unpin one first.
reference-empty: Pick a guide on the left, or search for a quest, a guide or an item. Clicking an item anywhere in the book opens its page here.
party-invite-hint: Pick a player below, then press Invite.
party-invite-nobody: Everyone online is already in your party.
problems-about: Found when the quests last loaded. A broken quest is left out of the book until it's fixed; warnings don't stop anything. Click a quest to edit it.
edit-no-chapter: There are no chapters here yet. Press New chapter to start one.
edit-hint: Right-click empty canvas to add a quest. Drag a quest to move it. Right-drag from one quest to another to make the first a prerequisite of the second; do it again to remove it. To set an item, click a slot while holding the item, or with it on the cursor.
edit-needs-nothing: Needs nothing: available from the start.
edit-link-hint: Right-drag from another quest to this one to add or remove a prerequisite.
edit-more: {0} more, not shown here. Edit them in the exported JSON.
edit-choice: A choice of {0} rewards (edit in JSON)
edit-loop: That would make a loop: the other quest already needs this one.
req-discovered: something you'll find on your own
plan-ready: Ready: you can get this now
plan-hidden: A step further back. It'll show once you get closer.
plan-hint-ready: Get this next. How is up to you: the handbook knows, and so does trying things.
plan-hint: Part of your plan. Hints show what to get, not how.
plan-unknown: Nothing in the game makes this. Look for it in the world.
